programmes.name_en: Creative Europe MEDIA strand
programmes.funder: European Commission (DG EAC / DG CNECT), implemented by EACEA
programmes.amount_note: Grant amounts differ per action. The programme landing page does not publish a budget figure or co-funding rate for 2021-2027, so both are null here. Actions most relevant to companies include Video Games and Immersive Content Development (CREA-MEDIA-2026-DEVVGIM) and European mini-slate development (CREA-MEDIA-2026-DEVMINISLATE); the specific amounts are in each call's guidelines.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual calls with fixed deadlines on the F&T Portal. 2027 MEDIA calls open since 29 Sep 2026: European slate development closes 30 Nov 2026; Innovative tools and business models 13 Jan 2027; Video games and immersive content 1 Feb 2027; co-development 1 Mar 2027. closes_at is the earliest open deadline.

procedure_steps.detail: Find the relevant CREA-MEDIA call on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.
Register your company and obtain a PIC.
Submit the single-stage proposal by the deadline. Contact your national Creative Europe Desk for guidance.

documents_required.doc: Application forms Part A and Part B
Company track record / previous works evidence
documents_required.note: Most MEDIA development actions require a prior production track record

documents_required.doc: Project development plan and budget

eligibility.other_note: 'The Creative Europe programme is divided into 2 strands, Culture and MEDIA, and is supported by a cross-sectoral strand.' The Video Games and Immersive Content Development action is 'Aimed at European video game development and XR/AR studios'. Most MEDIA calls require an established production company with a track record, which excludes brand-new startups.

programmes.source_snippet: The Creative Europe programme is divided into 2 strands, Culture and MEDIA, and is supported by a cross-sectoral strand.

programmes.name_en: Digital Europe Programme
programmes.funder: European Commission (DG CNECT), implemented by HaDEA and EISMEA
programmes.amount_note: Programme budget is 'over €8.1 billion' for the Multiannual Financial Framework 2021-2027. Grant sizes and co-funding rates are set per topic in the annual work programmes (typically 50% for most actions and higher for some, but this was not stated on the official programme page, so cofunding_pct is null here rather than guessed).
programmes.deadline_note: Calls published on the F&T Portal with topic-specific deadlines. Currently listed open: CYBER-11-DUALUSE, CYBER-11-EULEG and CYBER-11-NCC, 01-09-2026 to 14-01-2027.

procedure_steps.detail: Search the DIGITAL programme page on the Funding & Tenders Portal for open topics.
Register your organisation and obtain a PIC.
Submit the proposal by the topic deadline. Many DIGITAL topics fund consortia or European Digital Innovation Hubs, which then deliver free or subsidised services to SMEs.

documents_required.doc: Proposal Part A and Part B
PIC for every partner

eligibility.other_note: The programme 'supports industry, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and public administration in their digital transformation'. Thematic areas: 'supercomputing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, advanced digital skills, and ensuring a wide use of digital technologies across the economy and society', plus semiconductors added in September 2023. Important nuance for aggregators: much of the SME-facing value flows indirectly, via European Digital Innovation Hubs, whose services to an SME may themselves count as de minimis aid at national level.

programmes.source_snippet: With an overall budget of over €8.1 billion, DIGITAL aims to shape the digital transformation ... supercomputing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, advanced digital skills, and ensuring a wide use of digital technologies across the economy and society

programmes.name_en: European Innovation Council Business Acceleration Services
programmes.funder: European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA)
programmes.amount_note: No cash award. BAS provides in-kind support: coaching, mentoring, expertise and training, access to global corporate partners, investor matchmaking and ecosystem/peer access. The official page does not state a monetary value.
programmes.deadline_note: Open calls for individual services are published on the EIC Community Platform on a rolling basis. 'Our services have no expiration date. You remain eligible to apply even after your project has concluded.'

procedure_steps.detail: Visit the EIC Community Platform to view open BAS calls and submit applications.
Browse the EIC Service Catalogue for available partner services.

documents_required.doc: Proof of eligible status (EIC awardee, Step 1 applicant, Seal of Excellence holder, Women TechEU awardee, EIC Scaling Club member)

eligibility.other_note: Services are for EIC awardees (Pre-accelerator, Accelerator, Transition, Pathfinder, STEP Scale Up, SME Instrument/FET), EIC Scaling Club members, Seal of Excellence/STEP Seal holders, Women TechEU awardees and Ukrainian tech SMEs/startups. Not open to the general public.

programmes.source_snippet: EIC support goes far beyond funding. It provides to the EIC top-notch innovators with access to a range of tailor-made high-quality Business Acceleration Services (BAS). ... Our services have no expiration date. You remain eligible to apply even after your project has concluded.

programmes.name_en: European Innovation Council Pathfinder Challenges
programmes.funder: European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA) / European Commission, under Horizon Europe
programmes.amount_note: Same instrument as Pathfinder Open ('up to EUR 4 million or more if duly justified'), but proposals must address one of the pre-defined Challenge topics set in the annual EIC Work Programme. Unlike Pathfinder Open, single applicants are permitted. Booster grants of a fixed amount not exceeding EUR 50 000 are also available.
programmes.deadline_note: EIC Pathfinder Challenges 2026 deadline: 28 October 2026. Pathfinder Open 2026 deadline was 12 May 2026.

procedure_steps.detail: Check the Challenge topics in the current EIC Work Programme and confirm your project fits one of them.
Register on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and obtain a PIC.
Submit a single-stage full proposal by the annual deadline; single applicants are allowed under Challenges.

documents_required.doc: Proposal Part A (administrative forms, budget)
Proposal Part B (technical description addressing the specific Challenge)

eligibility.other_note: Single applicants (including a single SME or startup) are permitted for Pathfinder Challenges only. Proposals must address a pre-defined Challenge topic. Challenge topics for 2026 are set out in the EIC Work Programme 2026 (published 17 June 2026).

programmes.source_snippet: Single Applicants: Permitted for Pathfinder Challenges only ... Pathfinder Challenges: 28 October 2026

programmes.name_en: European Innovation Council Pre-Accelerator
programmes.funder: European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA) / European Commission, under the Horizon Europe Widening (WIDERA) work programme
programmes.amount_note: 'Individual grants between 500 thousand and 1 million EUR.' The 2025 call awarded up to EUR 500 000 per company (70 companies, ~EUR 32.5 million total). The next call under the WIDERA work programme 2026-2027 is stated to raise this to EUR 1 million per company with a EUR 40 million budget.
programmes.deadline_note: 2027 call opens 5 May 2027 and closes 18 November 2027. 2025 call has closed.

procedure_steps.detail: Check that your company is established in an eligible Horizon Europe Widening country or outermost region.
Register on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and obtain a PIC.
Submit a single-applicant SME proposal via the Funding & Tenders Portal when the call is open.

documents_required.doc: Proposal Part A and Part B
SME self-declaration / evidence of SME status
documents_required.note: SME status per Recommendation 2003/361/EC

eligibility.other_note: Single SMEs established in Horizon Europe widening countries (e.g. Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia) and specified associated countries. Grant covers 70% of eligible cost.

programmes.source_snippet: Individual grants between 500 thousand and 1 million EUR. Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, ...

programmes.name_en: European Innovation Council STEP Scale Up
programmes.funder: European Innovation Council Fund / EISMEA, under the Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform (STEP)
programmes.amount_note: 'offering financial support in the form of investments to startups, SMEs, and small mid-caps, between EUR 10 to 30 million'. Equity only - no grant component. 2026 budget: EUR 300 million.
programmes.deadline_note: The EIC states applicants 'can apply anytime via the Funding & Tenders Portal'; no fixed cut-off dates are published for the general STEP Scale Up call in 2026.

procedure_steps.detail: Secure proof of initial market interest from a qualified investor covering at least 20% of the total target funding round.
Register on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and obtain a PIC.
Submit the application at any time; evaluation, interview and due diligence follow.

documents_required.doc: Application form / business plan
Evidence of qualified investor interest covering at least 20% of the target round
Financial statements for due diligence

eligibility.other_note: 'A single SME or small mid-cap (fewer than 500 employees)' established in EU Member States or eligible Associated Countries (excluding the UK). Target sectors: digital and deep tech, clean technologies, biotechnologies. Requires 'proof of initial market interest from a qualified investor covering at least 20% of the total target funding round'.

programmes.source_snippet: The EIC STEP Scale Up scheme is part of the Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform (STEP), offering financial support in the form of investments to startups, SMEs, and small mid-caps, between EUR 10 to 30 million.

programmes.name_en: European Innovation Council STEP Scale Up Defence
programmes.funder: European Innovation Council Fund / EISMEA, under the Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform (STEP)
programmes.amount_note: EUR 10-30 million equity per company via the EIC Fund, designed to catalyse larger rounds of EUR 50-150 million or more. 2026 budget: EUR 100 million. No grant component.
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 application deadline: 28 October 2026. Interview notification 4-6 weeks from evaluation start; results 2 weeks after interview.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm eligibility: single SME or small mid-cap (<500 employees) in an EU Member State, an EEA country associated with Horizon Europe, or Ukraine, working on critical defence technologies.
Obtain proof of initial market interest from a single qualified investor covering at least 20% of the total target funding round.
Submit via the EU Funding & Tenders Portal by the deadline; interview and due diligence follow.

documents_required.doc: Application form / business plan
Evidence of qualified investor interest covering at least 20% of the target round

eligibility.other_note: Critical defence technology areas explicitly named include air and missile defence, drones and counter-drones. Eligible countries: EU Member States, EEA countries associated with Horizon Europe, and Ukraine. This scheme marks the EIC opening to defence and dual-use technologies from 17 June 2026.

programmes.source_snippet: breakthrough innovations in the critical defence technologies areas such as air and missile defence, drones and counter drones ... proof of initial market interest from a single qualified investor covering at least 20% of the total target funding round

programmes.name_en: European Innovation Council Transition
programmes.funder: European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA) / European Commission, under Horizon Europe
programmes.amount_note: 'Grants of up to EUR 2.5 million' to validate and demonstrate technology in an application-relevant environment and develop a business plan. Booster grants not exceeding EUR 50 000 are available for complementary activities. Non-dilutive; the specific funding rate is not stated on the EIC Transition page.
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 deadline was 16 September 2026 and has passed; 2027 dates not stated on the official page. 2026 budget EUR 100 million.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm your project builds on results from an eligible source project at experimental proof of concept (TRL 3 completed) or, ideally, technology validated in the lab (TRL 4).
Register on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and obtain a PIC.
Submit a single-stage full proposal by the annual deadline; remote evaluation followed by an interview for shortlisted proposals.

documents_required.doc: Proposal Part A and Part B
Evidence of the eligible source project results (TRL 3-4)
documents_required.note: Eligible sources include EIC Pathfinder, ERC Proof of Concept, Horizon Europe/Horizon 2020 Research and Innovation Actions, European Defence Fund projects (civil applications only) and Research Infrastructures projects

eligibility.other_note: Open to single entities (start-ups, SMEs, research organisations, universities), small consortia of minimum 2 legal entities from different Member States/Associated Countries, or multi-beneficiary consortia of 3-5 independent legal entities. Crucially, the project must build on results of a specific eligible prior project - you cannot enter EIC Transition from a standing start.

programmes.source_snippet: Grants of up to EUR 2.5 million ... experimental proof of concept (TRL 3 completed) or, ideally, technology validated in the lab level (TRL 4) ... Deadline for submissions: 16/09

programmes.name_en: EIT Food Accelerator Network
programmes.funder: EIT Food (European Institute of Innovation and Technology Knowledge and Innovation Community)
programmes.amount_note: Each startup receives a EUR 3 000 grant to cover travel expenses during the programme. At the end, each Hub runs a Tech Validation pitch event awarding three startups EUR 50 000 (1st), EUR 30 000 (2nd) and EUR 20 000 (3rd) to implement their tech validation project. Note: EIT Food's programme page describes this funding as being awarded through a SAFE (Simple Agreement For Future Equity) instrument, while the 2026 call page describes it as sub-grants for Technology Validation Projects - check the current call guidelines, as the instrument is material.
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 call closed 14 April 2026; next call not announced on the official page.

procedure_steps.detail: Choose the thematic Hub that matches your solution (six hubs: supply chains, circular solutions, biotech, agriculture, water systems, digital farming).
Submit the application by the annual deadline; selection into the accelerator programme follows.
Complete the programme and pitch at the Hub's Tech Validation event to compete for EUR 50 000 / 30 000 / 20 000.

documents_required.doc: Online application form
Proof of company registration in an eligible country
Financials evidencing revenue below EUR 1 million

eligibility.other_note: Pre-series A, revenue up to EUR 1 million, team of no more than 20, established in or after 2016, TRL 4-8, registered in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe-associated country (Switzerland and UK also eligible). Top three startups per hub receive EUR 50,000 / 30,000 / 20,000 for a 2027 technology validation project.

programmes.source_snippet: The EIT Food Accelerator Network programme offers a €3,000 grant for each startup to cover their travel expenses during the programme. Additionally, each startup is offered an opportunity to compete for funding of up to €50,000 to implement their tech validation project.

programmes.name_en: EIT Health start-up and acceleration programmes
programmes.funder: EIT Health (European Institute of Innovation and Technology Knowledge and Innovation Community)
programmes.amount_note: EIT Health runs a portfolio of bootcamps and acceleration programmes (Regulatory Pathways Bootcamp, MedTech Bootcamp, Patient Innovation Bootcamp, User Validation Labs, Wild Card, Women Entrepreneurship Bootcamp) plus funding instruments such as the Transformative Healthcare Instrument. Funding amounts are not stated on the programme overview page and vary by call, so they are recorded as null rather than guessed.
programmes.deadline_note: All listed EIT Health acceleration programmes (Catapult, Start-ups Meet Pharma, Open Innovation, Healthy Investment CEE, Venture Centre of Excellence) show 'Closed for applications'.

procedure_steps.detail: Register your organisation in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal to obtain a nine-digit PIC number (required for EIT Health funding calls such as the Transformative Healthcare Instrument).
Apply to the call via EIT Health's own application platform.

documents_required.doc: PIC number from the EU Funding & Tenders Portal
documents_required.note: Required for EIT Health funding calls

documents_required.doc: Application submitted on apply.eithealth.eu

eligibility.other_note: Programme-specific: e.g. Regulatory Pathways Bootcamp is for digital health or medical device solutions; MedTech Bootcamp for teams with a medtech solution; Patient Innovation Bootcamp for patients and caregivers; Women Entrepreneurship Bootcamp for women-led or co-led start-ups. Several bootcamps accept pre-incorporation teams.

programmes.source_snippet: A 10-week blended programme to understand the highly regulated pathway within the European healthcare system. ... A six-week online programme for teams with a medtech solution, looking for hands-on business training and personalised coaching.

programmes.name_en: EIT Jumpstarter
programmes.funder: European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT), delivered jointly by several EIT Knowledge and Innovation Communities
programmes.amount_note: A 7-month pre-acceleration programme. Winners compete for EUR 2 500, EUR 5 000 or EUR 10 000 in startup funding, and all participants receive a EUR 2 000 participation budget plus EUR 1 000 travel budget. Total programme funding EUR 240 000 for 2026.
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 applications closed 17 May 2026; next edition not announced on the official page.

procedure_steps.detail: Check the eligible countries and thematic categories in the Terms and Conditions.
Apply online with your early-stage idea by the annual deadline.
Complete the 7-month training and mentorship programme and pitch at the final for the prizes; teams are expected to be ready for company creation by the end.

documents_required.doc: Online application form describing the idea and team
Proof of citizenship/residence in an eligible country

eligibility.other_note: Applicants must be citizens of eligible EU widening/Horizon Europe associated countries or EU outermost regions (e.g. Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia, Spain, Albania, Serbia, Ukraine, Turkiye). Winners receive EUR 2,500, 5,000 or 10,000 plus EUR 2,000 stipend and EUR 1,000 travel budget.

programmes.source_snippet: EIT Jumpstarter is back with €240,000. Join the 2026 EIT Jumpstarter programme. ... A 7-month pre-acceleration programme for early-stage innovators from over 22 countries.

programmes.name_local: EIT Urban Mobility - Financial Support to Startups Open Call
programmes.name_en: EIT Urban Mobility Financial Support to Startups
programmes.funder: EIT Urban Mobility (European Institute of Innovation and Technology Knowledge and Innovation Community)
programmes.amount_note: 'EIT Urban Mobility will provide financial support of up to €2.5 million per company, for startups developing breakthrough mobility solutions.' The exact instrument mix (grant versus investment) and any co-financing requirement are set in the Call Manual, which is the binding document.
programmes.deadline_note: Cut-offs 23 Feb, 18 May, 31 Aug and 16 Nov 2026 (17:00 CET). Next: 16 November 2026. Companies cannot apply to three consecutive cut-offs.

procedure_steps.detail: Read the Call Manual for eligibility, special cases and the full cut-off schedule.
Submit the application via the EIT Urban Mobility open call page before the chosen cut-off.

documents_required.doc: Application form
Business plan / pitch materials
documents_required.note: Per the Call Manual

eligibility.other_note: Legal entities in EU Member States or associated third countries, currently fundraising (pre-seed/seed/Series A), urban mobility innovation, valuation not above EUR 50 million, founders holding over 40% equity, prototype/pilot/MVP, not already in EIT UM equity portfolio. EIT UM invests alongside VC or private investors and will not normally lead.

programmes.source_snippet: EIT Urban Mobility will provide financial support of up to €2.5 million per company, for startups developing breakthrough mobility solutions. Funding is provided through an open application process with multiple cut offs throughout 2026 ... Cut off 1 – 23 February 2026

programmes.name_en: BlueInvest (EMFAF blue economy investment readiness)
programmes.funder: European Commission (DG MARE / CINEA) with the European Investment Fund
programmes.amount_note: Two components: the BlueInvest readiness assistance programme (free coaching and investor matchmaking, no cash) and the BlueInvest Fund, an EIF equity mandate investing in VC funds that back blue economy companies. Separate EMFAF grant calls fund blue economy innovation projects with budgets set per call.
programmes.deadline_note: Readiness assistance runs in cohorts with periodic application windows; EMFAF blue economy grant calls are published annually by CINEA.

eligibility.other_note: Blue economy companies (aquaculture, ocean energy, marine biotech, maritime digitalisation, coastal resilience) established in the EU.

programmes.name_en: CASSINI Space Entrepreneurship Initiative (myEUspace, Business Accelerator, Prizes, Seed and Growth Funding)
programmes.funder: European Commission (DG DEFIS) with EUSPA and the European Investment Fund
programmes.amount_note: Umbrella of instruments for space start-ups: the myEUspace competition (cash prizes to teams developing apps using Galileo/EGNOS/Copernicus, historically in the tens of thousands of euro per winner, awarded in stages), the CASSINI Business Accelerator (equity-free acceleration, no cash), CASSINI Prizes/Challenges and the CASSINI Seed and Growth Funding facility, a EUR 1 billion EIF-managed equity facility investing via VC funds into space and dual-use companies.
programmes.deadline_note: Each CASSINI strand has its own cycle. myEUspace and the CASSINI Challenges have run as annual competitions; the Business Accelerator recruits in cohorts; the equity facility invests continuously through EIF-selected funds.

eligibility.other_note: Start-ups and SMEs in EU Member States using EU Space Programme data and signals (Galileo, EGNOS, Copernicus, GOVSATCOM). Some strands accept pre-incorporation teams and individuals.

programmes.name_en: Circular Bio-based Europe Joint Undertaking (CBE JU)
programmes.funder: Circular Bio-based Europe Joint Undertaking (CBE JU)
programmes.amount_note: Institutionalised European Partnership under Horizon Europe. Calls fund collaborative R&I projects, typically EUR 2-30 million each. Funding rates follow Horizon Europe rules (100% for RIA, 70% for for-profit participants in Innovation Actions). Some JUs additionally require private members to match with in-kind contributions.
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 call (EUR 170.7 million, 13 topics) closed 22 September 2026; 2027 call not announced on the page.
programmes.reopen_note: Each Joint Undertaking publishes an annual work programme setting the next call dates; check the JU website for the current calendar.

eligibility.other_note: Consortium requirements as in Horizon Europe. SMEs and start-ups participate as consortium partners; some JUs give SMEs a higher funding rate or reserved budget. Membership of the JU's private association is not required to apply but is common among coordinators.

programmes.name_en: EU Chips Act national semiconductor competence centres
programmes.funder: Chips Joint Undertaking and national governments
programmes.amount_note: Each Member State hosts a competence centre offering startups and SMEs design tool access, expertise, training and support in reaching the pilot lines. Services are subsidised; some centres also run small voucher schemes.
programmes.deadline_note: Competence centres operate continuously; individual voucher schemes have their own deadlines.

programmes.name_en: Chips Joint Undertaking (formerly KDT JU)
programmes.amount_note: Institutionalised European Partnership under Horizon Europe. Calls fund collaborative R&I projects, typically EUR 2-30 million each. Funding rates follow Horizon Europe rules (100% for RIA, 70% for for-profit participants in Innovation Actions). Some JUs additionally require private members to match with in-kind contributions.
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 Chips JU calls opened 7 July 2026; AI chip demonstrators and AI compute evaluation platform close 27 Oct 2026; EU-Japan collaboration closes 8 Dec 2026.
programmes.reopen_note: Each Joint Undertaking publishes an annual work programme setting the next call dates; check the JU website for the current calendar.

eligibility.other_note: Consortium requirements as in Horizon Europe. SMEs and start-ups participate as consortium partners; some JUs give SMEs a higher funding rate or reserved budget. Membership of the JU's private association is not required to apply but is common among coordinators.

programmes.name_en: EU Chips Act - Chips Joint Undertaking calls for proposals
programmes.funder: Chips Joint Undertaking (European Commission, Participating States, AENEAS, EPoSS and INSIDE Industry Association)
programmes.amount_note: Multiple calls opened on 7 July 2026 totalling over EUR 300 million, covering AI hardware, edge computing, cybersecurity, 6G, power electronics, photonics and health applications. EU funding is combined with national co-funding from Participating States.
programmes.deadline_note: Calls opened 7 July 2026 (16 calls, over EUR 300 million). Open: AI chip demonstrators and AI compute evaluation platform close 27 Oct 2026; EU-Japan semiconductor collaboration closes 8 Dec 2026. Earlier 16-17 Sep dates were incorrect for these calls.
programmes.reopen_note: Usually reopens around July or September (annual call).

eligibility.other_note: Consortium-based; startups participate as partners. National co-funding rules from the relevant Participating State apply on top of the EU contribution.

programmes.source_snippet: the European public-private partnership that promotes the development and adoption of advanced nano-electronic chip technologies and systems manufactured in Europe

programmes.name_local: Chips for Europe Initiative pilot lines
programmes.name_en: EU Chips Act pilot lines access for startups
programmes.amount_note: Access to advanced semiconductor pilot lines (FD-SOI, sub-2nm, heterogeneous integration, wide bandgap) and design platforms. Access for startups and SMEs is typically subsidised rather than paid as a cash grant.
programmes.deadline_note: Pilot lines opened progressively from 2024 onwards; access is arranged through the pilot line operators and national competence centres.

eligibility.other_note: The Chips for Europe Initiative supports technological capacity building through pilot lines, design platforms, competence centres and skills development.

programmes.source_snippet: Chips for Europe Initiative: Supports technological capacity building through pilot lines, design platforms, competence centers, and skills development

programmes.name_en: Clean Aviation Joint Undertaking
programmes.amount_note: Institutionalised European Partnership under Horizon Europe. Calls fund collaborative R&I projects, typically EUR 2-30 million each. Funding rates follow Horizon Europe rules (100% for RIA, 70% for for-profit participants in Innovation Actions). Some JUs additionally require private members to match with in-kind contributions.
programmes.deadline_note: Next call (Call 5): topics expected end of December 2026, official launch early 2027.
programmes.reopen_note: Call 5 topics release end of December 2026; launch early 2027.

eligibility.other_note: Consortium requirements as in Horizon Europe. SMEs and start-ups participate as consortium partners; some JUs give SMEs a higher funding rate or reserved budget. Membership of the JU's private association is not required to apply but is common among coordinators.

programmes.name_en: Clean Hydrogen Joint Undertaking
programmes.amount_note: Institutionalised European Partnership under Horizon Europe. Calls fund collaborative R&I projects, typically EUR 2-30 million each. Funding rates follow Horizon Europe rules (100% for RIA, 70% for for-profit participants in Innovation Actions). Some JUs additionally require private members to match with in-kind contributions.
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 call (EUR 105 million, 21 topics) closed 15 April 2026 with 170 proposals; next call not announced.
programmes.reopen_note: Each Joint Undertaking publishes an annual work programme setting the next call dates; check the JU website for the current calendar.

eligibility.other_note: Consortium requirements as in Horizon Europe. SMEs and start-ups participate as consortium partners; some JUs give SMEs a higher funding rate or reserved budget. Membership of the JU's private association is not required to apply but is common among coordinators.

programmes.name_en: Creative Europe Cross-sectoral strand (incl. Innovation Lab, Journalism Partnerships)
programmes.amount_note: Covers the Creative Innovation Lab (cross-sector innovation between audiovisual, culture and other sectors), Journalism Partnerships and News Media support. Co-funding is typically up to 70-80% of eligible costs; budgets are set per call.
programmes.deadline_note: 2027 plans include a new edition of Creative Innovation Labs; no call dates published yet.
programmes.reopen_note: Re-issued each year under the annual Creative Europe work programme.

eligibility.other_note: Consortia of organisations from Creative Europe countries; creative-tech SMEs are eligible partners and are explicitly targeted by the Innovation Lab.

programmes.name_en: Creative Europe Culture strand
programmes.amount_note: European Cooperation Projects are funded at up to 80% of eligible costs, with three categories: small-scale (up to EUR 200,000), medium-scale (up to EUR 1 million) and large-scale (up to EUR 2 million). Separate schemes cover literary translation, networks and platforms, and mobility (Culture Moves Europe).
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 European Cooperation Projects call closed 5 May 2026. 2027 call (EUR 61 million) to be published in Q1 2027.
programmes.reopen_note: 2027 European Cooperation Projects call (EUR 61 million) to be published in Q1 2027.

eligibility.other_note: Cultural and creative organisations (including creative SMEs) legally established in a Creative Europe country. Small-scale projects need at least 3 partners from 3 countries; larger categories need more.

programmes.name_local: Creative Europe MEDIA - Innovative Tools and Business Models
programmes.name_en: Creative Europe MEDIA Innovative Tools and Business Models
programmes.amount_note: Grants for technology and business model innovation across the audiovisual value chain, covering up to 70% of eligible costs. Project budgets commonly run to several hundred thousand euro.
programmes.deadline_note: CREA-MEDIA-2027-INNOVBUSMOD: open 29 Sep 2026, single-stage, deadline 13 Jan 2027.

eligibility.other_note: Companies established in a Creative Europe participating country; consortium applications are common but single applicants are eligible for some topics.

programmes.name_local: Creative Europe MEDIA - European Slate Development
programmes.name_en: Creative Europe MEDIA European Slate Development support
programmes.amount_note: Lump sum support for the development of a slate of three to five audiovisual projects, historically in the range of EUR 60,000 to EUR 300,000 per slate at up to 50% of eligible costs.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual call, historically with a deadline in the autumn or early in the year.

eligibility.other_note: Independent European audiovisual production companies with a recent track record; established in a Creative Europe participating country.

programmes.name_local: Creative Europe MEDIA - European Video Games and Immersive Content Development
programmes.name_en: Creative Europe MEDIA video games and immersive content development support
programmes.funder: European Commission / European Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA)
programmes.amount_note: Lump sum grants for the development phase of video games, XR and immersive projects. Historically EUR 10,000 to EUR 300,000 per project depending on the total development budget, capped at 50% of eligible costs.
programmes.deadline_note: CREA-MEDIA-2027-DEVVGIM: open 29 Sep 2026, single-stage, deadline 1 Feb 2027.

eligibility.other_note: European production companies established in a Creative Europe participating country, majority-owned by nationals of participating countries, with a track record of a previously released work.

programmes.source_snippet: The MEDIA strand of the Creative Europe programme supports the European film and audiovisual industries to develop, distribute and promote European works, taking into account today's digital environment.

programmes.name_local: ESF+ EaSI strand - social economy and social innovation
programmes.name_en: EU ESF+ Employment and Social Innovation (EaSI) strand
programmes.funder: European Commission (DG EMPL) via EISMEA and the EU Programme for Employment and Social Innovation
programmes.amount_note: Calls supporting social economy ecosystems, social enterprise finance and social innovation. Grants normally cover up to 80-90% of eligible costs; project sizes commonly range from a few hundred thousand to a few million euro.
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 ESF+ social economy calls: networks call 6 Mar-19 Jun 2026; Inclusive Incubation and Finance (ESF-2026-SE-INCUBATION) closed 2 Sep 2026. No open call found.

eligibility.other_note: Applicants are usually public bodies, social economy networks or intermediaries rather than individual social enterprises; social enterprises benefit as end recipients. The InvestEU Social Investment and Skills window provides complementary guarantees to lenders.

programmes.name_en: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIH) services for SMEs
programmes.funder: European Commission (Digital Europe Programme) and national co-funding
programmes.amount_note: No cash to the SME. EDIHs provide 'test before invest' services, AI/HPC/cybersecurity experimentation, digital skills training and innovation-ecosystem access, delivered free or heavily subsidised under de minimis rules. Value per SME is capped by state-aid rules rather than a published grant amount.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous. SMEs approach their nearest EDIH directly; each hub has its own intake process.

eligibility.other_note: SMEs and public sector organisations located in the EDIH's region. Services are subsidised under de minimis state aid, so prior de minimis aid received counts against the ceiling.

programmes.name_en: European Innovation Council Accelerator
programmes.amount_note: Up to EUR 2.5 million grant for technology development and market readiness, combined with an optional EIC Fund equity investment (typically EUR 0.5-10 million, and up to EUR 15 million in some cases) through 'blended finance'.
programmes.deadline_note: EIC Accelerator 2026 cut-offs at 17:00 Brussels time: 7 Jan, 4 Mar, 6 May, 8 Jul, 2 Sep, 4 Nov 2026. The 2 Sep 2026 cut-off has passed; next cut-off 4 November 2026.

procedure_steps.detail: Submit the short application (pitch deck, video and form) at any time via the EIC AI platform
If successful, submit a full proposal before one of the published cut-offs
Face-to-face (or remote) jury interview for shortlisted companies
Grant agreement preparation and, for blended finance, EIC Fund due diligence

documents_required.doc: Short application form
Pitch deck
Video pitch
Full business plan (Annex)
Company financials

eligibility.other_note: Single SMEs (including startups and small mid-caps for the investment component) established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe associated country. Technology must be at TRL 5-8 for the grant.

programmes.source_snippet: EIC Accelerator: Scale-Up Grants & Investments for scaling up business. Deadlines: 7.01.2026 | 4.03.2026 | 6.05.2026 | 8.07.2026 | 2.09.2026 | 4.11.2026

programmes.name_en: EIC Accelerator Challenges (thematic calls)
programmes.amount_note: Same instrument as EIC Accelerator Open (grant up to EUR 2.5m lump sum, optional EUR 1-10m equity) but restricted to named strategic technology Challenges. 2026 budget for Challenges EUR 220 million.
programmes.deadline_note: EIC Accelerator 2026 cut-offs at 17:00 Brussels time: 7 Jan, 4 Mar, 6 May, 8 Jul, 2 Sep, 4 Nov 2026. The 2 Sep 2026 cut-off has passed; next cut-off 4 November 2026.

procedure_steps.detail: Check the Challenge topics published in the annual EIC Work Programme
Submit short proposal selecting the relevant Challenge
Full proposal at a Challenge-specific cut-off
EIC Jury interview
Grant agreement / investment due diligence

eligibility.other_note: Proposal must fall inside a named Challenge for that year's work programme. Same SME/small mid-cap eligibility as the Open track.

programmes.source_snippet: EUR 220 million to Accelerator Challenges and EUR 414 million to the Accelerator Open track

programmes.name_en: European Innovation Council Fund (direct equity)
programmes.funder: European Innovation Council Fund (managed by EIF/Alter Domus on behalf of the European Commission)
programmes.amount_note: Direct equity/quasi-equity. Standard EIC Accelerator blended-finance ticket is EUR 1-10 million. Under the STEP Scale-Up strand tickets of up to EUR 30 million are possible. The EIC Fund typically takes a 10-20% minority stake and does not seek control.
programmes.deadline_note: No separate application: companies access the EIC Fund by being selected through the EIC Accelerator or the EIC Scale-Up strand.

eligibility.other_note: Only companies selected via EIC Accelerator / EIC Scale-Up. Investment is subject to due diligence and to EU ownership and control screening.

programmes.name_en: European Innovation Council Pathfinder
programmes.amount_note: Standard grants up to EUR 4 million or more if duly justified; Booster grants fixed amount not exceeding EUR 50,000.
programmes.deadline_note: Pathfinder Open 2026 deadline 12 May 2026 (passed). Pathfinder Challenges 2026 deadline 28 October 2026.

eligibility.other_note: Pathfinder Open requires consortia of at least three independent legal entities (one in a Member State, two others in different Member States/Associated Countries). Challenges also allow single applicants and two-partner consortia.

programmes.source_snippet: up to EUR 4 million or more if duly justified ... at least three different independent legal entities ... At least one legal entity established in a Member State ... At least two other independent legal entities, each established in different Member States or Associated Countries

programmes.name_en: EIC Prizes (incl. European Innovation Procurement Awards)
programmes.amount_note: Prize amounts are not stated on the EIC prizes landing page.
programmes.deadline_note: Official EIC prizes page lists the European Capital of Innovation Awards, the European Prize for Women Innovators and previous prizes; no open contest with a deadline is shown.
programmes.reopen_note: New prize contests are announced with each EIC Work Programme; check the EIC prizes page for currently open contests.

eligibility.other_note: Eligibility is contest-specific; most EIC prizes are open to legal entities established in the EU or a Horizon Europe associated country.

programmes.name_en: Horizon Europe European Innovation Ecosystems, CONNECT strand
programmes.amount_note: Coordination and Support Actions plus Innovation Actions connecting regional innovation ecosystems. Project budgets typically EUR 1-6 million per topic. Several CONNECT projects run cascade funding (financial support to third parties) that re-grants to start-ups, commonly in the EUR 10,000-60,000 range per company.
programmes.deadline_note: HORIZON-EIE-2026-01 CONNECT-03 closed 20 January 2026 (budget EUR 4.5 million). Next EIE call (European Startup and Scaleup Hubs) opens October 2026.

eligibility.other_note: Direct applicants are typically consortia of ecosystem actors (clusters, agencies, incubators, universities). Start-ups usually benefit via the funded projects' cascade calls.

programmes.source_snippet: Scaling up deep tech ecosystems (HORIZON-EIE-2026-01-CONNECT-03)

programmes.name_en: Horizon Europe European Innovation Ecosystems, SCALEUP strand
programmes.amount_note: Supports the scale-up of innovation ecosystems and instruments such as Women TechEU and innovation procurement support. Budgets per topic are published in the EIE work programme; many actions include financial support to third parties passed on to start-ups.
programmes.deadline_note: EIE Work Programme 2026-2027: European Startup and Scaleup Hubs call opens October 2026; info webinar 22 October 2026.
programmes.reopen_note: European Startup and Scaleup Hubs call opens October 2026.

eligibility.other_note: Consortium-based. Deep-tech scale-ups can be direct partners in some topics and cascade beneficiaries in others.

programmes.name_local: EIF equity investments in VC and business angel funds
programmes.name_en: European Investment Fund equity mandates (InvestEU, ESCALAR, EIC Fund fund-of-funds)
programmes.amount_note: The EIF invests as a limited partner in venture capital funds, business angel co-investment vehicles and technology transfer funds rather than in start-ups directly. Founders benefit indirectly: a large share of European seed and Series A funds are EIF-backed. Ticket sizes into funds run from single-digit to hundreds of millions of euro.
programmes.deadline_note: EIF publishes calls for intermediaries; InvestEU equity products call deadline 30 June 2027.

eligibility.other_note: Direct applicants must be fund managers or financial intermediaries, not start-ups. Start-ups receive EIF money through the funds it backs.

programmes.name_en: EIT Climate-KIC Climate Entrepreneurship / Accelerator
programmes.amount_note: EIT Climate-KIC has historically run a staged accelerator paying equity-free grants per stage (commonly EUR 15,000 at Stage 1, EUR 25,000 Stage 2, EUR 50,000 Stage 3) plus coaching. The flagship pan-European Accelerator has been restructured into regional and challenge-led entrepreneurship programmes; check current offers.
programmes.deadline_note: The classic three-stage EIT Climate-KIC Accelerator is no longer offered as a single pan-European call; entrepreneurship support now runs through regional hubs, ClimAccelerator-branded programmes and challenge calls with their own deadlines.
programmes.reopen_note: ClimAccelerator programmes are launched by regional partners at different times of year; browse climate-kic.org opportunities for the currently open ones.

eligibility.other_note: Climate-impact start-ups; specific eligibility set by each regional ClimAccelerator.

programmes.name_en: EIT Climate-KIC ClimAccelerator
programmes.amount_note: Funding depends on resources of the delivery partner; Climate KIC offers in-kind support to high-impact start-ups in exchange for future equity (SAFE).
programmes.deadline_note: Applications for ClimAccelerators are on a rolling basis via local delivery partners.

eligibility.other_note: Programmes are typically restricted to teams based in the EU Member State or region hosting the individual ClimAccelerator.

programmes.source_snippet: Climate entrepreneurship is listed among EIT Climate-KIC focus areas; specific accelerator calls are published under the organisation's open calls section.

programmes.name_en: EIT Culture & Creativity start-up support
programmes.amount_note: Innovation Projects call: up to EUR 10.5M total, up to 11 projects. Stage 1 selected applicants receive EUR 20,000 to build a Business Development Plan; stage 2 implementation up to 18 months with up to EUR 900,000 per project.
programmes.deadline_note: Innovation Projects call, stage 1 closes 30 Oct 2026; stage 2 application form shared with selected applicants mid-Dec 2026 and open until 15 Mar 2027.

eligibility.other_note: Single legal entity (startup, scale-up or SME) in fashion, architecture or audiovisual media, established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe associated country, with a technically validated prototype/solution at TRL7.

programmes.source_snippet: Applications close on 30 October 2026 for stage 1. The application form for stage 2 will be shared with selected applicants in mid-December 2026 and will be open until 15 March 2027.

programmes.name_en: EIT Digital Venture Programme / Venture Incubation
programmes.amount_note: Venture Incubation Program 2026: EUR 5,000 Growth Package Prize after a 12-week incubation, then compete for up to EUR 25,000 final prize. Selected ventures give 28DIGITAL 5% equity via a SAFE.
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 edition closed 9 June 2026 17:00 Brussels time.
programmes.reopen_note: No 2027 edition announced on the page; monitor 28digital.eu.

eligibility.other_note: Teams of at least two members or startups incorporated 1 Jan 2025 or later, in an EU Member State or Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Turkiye or Ukraine; digital/deep-tech with prototype, PoC or near-MVP; one application per team.

programmes.source_snippet: Applications closing on 9 June 2026 at 17:00 (Brussels time). Selected ventures will commit to providing 28DIGITAL with 5% equity through a SAFE.

programmes.name_en: EIT Food Seedbed Venture Catalyst (formerly Seedbed Incubator)
programmes.amount_note: Catalytic 'smart funding' for early-stage costs such as IP licensing, prototyping or first hires, delivered with venture-builder support. Amounts not published on the page.
programmes.deadline_note: No central call dates published; Seedbed Venture Catalyst is delivered through partner venture builders (Carbon13, Enviu, FOOD FOUNDERS Studio, Fresh Ventures Studio, Ivoro Ventures, Kost Studio, Zinc).
programmes.reopen_note: Contact the partner venture builders listed on the Seedbed page for intake dates.

eligibility.other_note: Researchers, technology owners and aspiring founders in agrifood, supported via partner venture builders (venture-builder programmes decide intake).

programmes.source_snippet: Seedbed Venture Catalyst is a partnership with Europe's leading Venture Building programmes, offering catalytic funding to ambitious founding teams so they can overcome blockers on their journey.

programmes.name_en: EIT Health Catapult
programmes.amount_note: Life sciences and health tech winners each receive a EUR 30,000 cash prize; cash prize up to EUR 30,000 plus in-kind industry prizes; Audience Award winner shown on the NY Nasdaq Tower.
programmes.deadline_note: 10th edition application phase closed; finalists pitch end November at the EIT Health Flagship Event.
programmes.reopen_note: Catapult runs annually; the next application window is announced on eithealth.eu, usually in spring.

eligibility.other_note: Micro or small enterprise (<50 employees) in Life Sciences or HealthTech, incorporated and operating in an EU/Horizon Europe associated country, incorporated no more than 10 years ago, with at least EUR 500,000 private investment or revenue, seeking at least EUR 2M funding; proposals in English.

programmes.source_snippet: The Application Phase has been closed stay tuned for programme updates. The life sciences and the health tech winner receive a EUR 30,000 cash prize each.

programmes.name_en: EIT Health Headstart
programmes.amount_note: Equity-free grant of up to EUR 75,000 per start-up to reach a defined commercial milestone (regulatory, clinical validation, market entry). Awarded through regional EIT Health InnoStars/CLC calls.
programmes.deadline_note: Ended: Headstart page no longer exists on eithealth.eu and the programme is not among the 45 current programmes; EIT Health now funds start-ups via calls such as Innovation Uptake and Innovation Validation.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify your EIT Health regional office (CLC or InnoStars)
Submit the application form with a milestone-based work plan and budget
Jury pitch/interview
Grant agreement and milestone-based payment

documents_required.doc: Business plan / commercialisation plan
Milestone and budget plan
Company registration documents

eligibility.other_note: Health, medtech, biotech or digital health start-up registered in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe associated country. Some rounds require the company to be an EIT Health alumnus or partner-nominated.

programmes.name_en: EIT Health Innovation Uptake Call
programmes.amount_note: Total budget up to EUR 5.2M for up to 8 projects; max EUR 650,000 per project; funds up to 50% of total project costs; SMEs leading projects receive EUR 400,000-500,000 within the grant.
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 call opened 24 Jun 2026 and closed 16 Sep 2026.
programmes.reopen_note: Next call not announced.

eligibility.other_note: Consortium of at least two independent legal entities from different countries, spanning at least two sides of the Knowledge Triangle, led by a commercialising SME or industry entity; mature digital/AI healthcare solutions; entities in eligible Horizon Europe countries.

programmes.source_snippet: Maximum funding per project: EUR 650,000. Funding covers up to 50% of total project costs (co-funding required). Call closes on: 16 September 2026.

programmes.name_en: EIT Health Innovation Validation Call
programmes.amount_note: EIT Health funds up to 50% of total project budget, up to EUR 850,000 per project, up to 24 months; micro/small commercialising enterprises must receive EUR 400,000-500,000 of the grant.
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 call opened 25 Feb 2026 and closed 6 May 2026.
programmes.reopen_note: Next call not announced.

eligibility.other_note: Consortium of at least two organisations from different countries covering two sides of the Knowledge Triangle, led by a commercialising company; digital or AI-enabled medical devices (MDR/IVDR) at Innovation Maturity Level 6.

programmes.source_snippet: EIT Health will fund up to 50% of the total project budget, up to a total grant funding amount of EUR 850,000 per project. Call closes on: 6 May 2026.

programmes.name_en: EIT HEI Initiative: Innovation Capacity Building for Higher Education
programmes.funder: EIT (implemented by EIT RawMaterials on behalf of the EIT Community)
programmes.amount_note: Call for Proposals 2026 pre-announced: up to EUR 1.25 million per project (CfP 2025 offered up to EUR 2 million). Funds higher education institutions, not start-ups directly.
programmes.deadline_note: New Call for Proposals to launch in Q4 2026; deadline to be announced.
programmes.reopen_note: Call for Proposals 2026 pre-announced, launch Q4 2026.

eligibility.other_note: Applicants are higher education institutions in consortia (min. 3 HEIs from 3 countries plus non-HEI partners). Start-ups benefit indirectly via university support services.

programmes.source_snippet: The EIT Higher Education Initiative (EIT HEI) will launch its new Call for Proposals in Q4 2026 to support higher education institutions (HEIs)... Up to EUR 1.25 million per project. Deadline: To be announced.

programmes.name_en: EIT InnoEnergy Highway
programmes.amount_note: EIT InnoEnergy invests in sustainable-energy start-ups and takes an equity stake, alongside a business acceleration package (market access, industrial partners, recruitment). Ticket sizes are negotiated per company and are not published as a fixed figure; InnoEnergy typically invests at seed and Series A.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling application through the InnoEnergy Highway intake form; assessment runs continuously with periodic investment committees.

eligibility.other_note: Clean-tech/clean-energy-transition companies with at least a proof of concept or prototype, early-stage, mainly Europe but also USA and Japan.

programmes.source_snippet: Our focus is on: A complementary, diverse and execution-driven team; Fields related to clean tech; Companies with at least a proof of concept/prototype; Early-stage development; Mainly Europe, but also USA and Japan.

programmes.name_en: EIT InnoEnergy startup investment and support
programmes.amount_note: Combination of equity investment and in-kind business acceleration. Ticket sizes are negotiated case by case and are not published.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications accepted on a rolling basis through the InnoEnergy startup application form.

procedure_steps.detail: Submit the online startup application form describing the technology, team and market
Screening and due diligence by an InnoEnergy thematic team
Investment committee decision; support delivered as capital plus access to the InnoEnergy industrial network

eligibility.other_note: Focus areas include energy storage, transport and mobility, decarbonising industry, smart grids and renewable energy. Created in 2010 by the European Institute of Innovation and Technology; network of over 1,400 partners.

programmes.source_snippet: We invest in people with high-impact solutions advancing the clean energy transition. Mainly Europe, but also USA and Japan.

programmes.name_en: EIT Manufacturing BoostUp! competition
programmes.amount_note: Pan-European competition with regional heats and a European final, in Create / Grow / Expand categories. Winners receive cash prizes (historically in the EUR 10,000-50,000 range per category) plus access to EIT Manufacturing's industrial network. Equity-free.
programmes.deadline_note: Ended: EIT Manufacturing was liquidated in March 2026; eitmanufacturing.eu now redirects to eit.europa.eu.

eligibility.other_note: Start-ups, scale-ups and innovators with manufacturing-related solutions from EIT Manufacturing's regional coverage.

programmes.name_en: EIT RawMaterials Booster Call
programmes.amount_note: ERMA Booster Call: tickets up to EUR 2.5M; start-ups up to EUR 0.5M, scale-ups/SMEs up to EUR 1.5M, mining and recycling projects up to EUR 2.5M. EIT RawMaterials invests directly.
programmes.deadline_note: Call is closed; updates will be published on the page.
programmes.reopen_note: The Booster call has been repeated annually; EIT RawMaterials announces the next edition on eitrawmaterials.eu.

eligibility.other_note: Start-ups: seed stage, TRL4+; scale-ups/SMEs: late seed to Series A, TRL8 and CRL8 minimum, at least EUR 200k commercial revenue; mining/recycling projects relevant to EU critical raw materials supply.

programmes.source_snippet: Eligible Start-ups ... can receive funding up to EUR 0.5m. Eligible Scale-Ups, and SMEs ... up to EUR 1.5m. Eligible mining projects, and recycling projects ... up to EUR 2.5m. Call closed.

programmes.name_en: EIT Urban Mobility Accelerator
programmes.amount_note: Techstars x EIT Urban Mobility Founder Catalyst: SAFE of EUR 50,000 (EUR 10,000 cash plus EUR 40,000 programme services), plus an extra EUR 50,000 investment if post-programme milestones are met. Not equity-free (SAFE).
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 cohort open call ran 30 Jun - 26 Aug 2026; programme starts late Sept 2026, demo day 3 Dec 2026.
programmes.reopen_note: Programme runs three cohorts over three years (Cohort 1 = 2026); next cohort dates not announced.

eligibility.other_note: Early-stage (pre-seed) for-profit urban-mobility startups with early traction, legally incorporated in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe associated country; previous Techstars/EIT UM accelerator participants generally ineligible.

programmes.source_snippet: Participating startups receive an initial EUR 10,000 investment, with the chance to unlock an additional EUR 50,000 by hitting agreed milestones. Applications closed.

programmes.name_en: EIT Water (Knowledge and Innovation Community)
programmes.funder: EIT Water / European Institute of Innovation and Technology
programmes.amount_note: Newest EIT Innovation Community, designated in 2025 to address water resilience. Its start-up-facing instruments (acceleration, incubation, business creation calls) are being rolled out; funding amounts are not yet published as standing figures.
programmes.deadline_note: Ended: the EIT call to create the EIT Water community is closed (consortium selected Nov 2025); no start-up-facing call found on the official page.

eligibility.other_note: Water resilience, water treatment, water reuse and water-in-industry innovators in the EU and Horizon Europe associated countries.

programmes.source_snippet: EIT Water Launched: New Innovation Community to Tackle Europe's Water Challenges

programmes.name_en: Enterprise Europe Network (EEN)
programmes.funder: European Commission (EISMEA), Single Market Programme, with national co-funding
programmes.amount_note: Free of charge to the SME. Services include international partner search and brokerage, the partnering opportunities database, EU funding advice, IP and regulatory guidance, and the Enhancing SME Innovation Management Capacity service (a multi-day free consultancy engagement). No cash is paid to the company.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous. Contact your local EEN partner organisation (usually a chamber of commerce, regional development agency or technology centre) at any time.

procedure_steps.detail: Find your local EEN contact point using the network search on een.ec.europa.eu
Request an initial diagnostic meeting
Agree an action plan (partner search, funding advice, innovation management support)
Publish or search partnering profiles in the EEN database

eligibility.other_note: SMEs established in an EEN participating country (all EU Member States plus many third countries). Free at the point of use.

programmes.source_snippet: The world's largest support network for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) with international ambitions. We identify EU funding opportunities that suit your business' needs and help you apply.

programmes.name_local: ERA-NET Cofund and co-funded European Partnerships
programmes.name_en: ERA-NET Cofund / co-funded European Partnership transnational calls
programmes.funder: Consortia of national research funding agencies, co-funded by the European Commission under Horizon Europe
programmes.amount_note: Transnational joint calls where each partner is paid by its own national agency at national rates (SME rates commonly 50-70%). Typical project budgets are EUR 0.5-2 million across the consortium. Examples of active partnership families: Driving Urban Transitions, Water4All, Biodiversa+, CETPartnership, Chemicals Risk Assessment, Transforming Health and Care Systems.
programmes.deadline_note: Each partnership issues its own annual or biennial joint call, most with a two-stage pre-proposal/full-proposal structure. Deadlines are scattered across the year; ERA-LEARN maintains the consolidated calendar.

procedure_steps.detail: Find an open joint call on ERA-LEARN or the partnership website
Check your own country's national eligibility annex and funding rate - these differ sharply between agencies
Form a transnational consortium meeting the call's minimum country requirement
Submit the joint pre-proposal, then the full proposal if invited
National funding decisions and national grant agreements

eligibility.other_note: Consortium of partners from at least two or three participating countries. National annexes decide whether companies (as opposed to research organisations) are fundable in your country - in some agencies SMEs are excluded from specific calls.

programmes.source_snippet: Partnerships ... Showing 159 partnerships (Horizon Europe Co-funded Partnership, Co-programmed Partnership, Institutionalised Partnerships).

programmes.name_en: Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs (EYE)
programmes.amount_note: Monthly financial assistance to new entrepreneurs to cover travel and subsistence during a 1-6 month stay with an experienced entrepreneur abroad. The monthly rate is set per host country and published in the country table; it is a contribution to costs, not a business grant.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous open application through the EYE online tool; matching happens on a rolling basis via local intermediary organisations.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on the Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs online platform
Get validated by a local intermediary organisation
Search for and agree a match with a host entrepreneur abroad
Sign the commitment to quality and the financial agreement
Complete the exchange and reporting

eligibility.other_note: New entrepreneurs must either have a firm intention to start a business or have started one within the last three years, and be permanently resident in a participating country. Hosts must run an SME with more than three years' experience.

programmes.source_snippet: New entrepreneurs, firmly planning to set up their own business or have already started one within the last three years. No fees to participate in the programme!

programmes.name_en: ESA BIC (European Space Agency Business Incubation Centres)
programmes.funder: European Space Agency with national and regional co-funding partners
programmes.amount_note: EUR 50k equity-free funding for product and IP development plus up to two years of incubation, technical support from ESA experts, business coaching, legal/IPR advice and fundraising guidance.
programmes.deadline_note: Each ESA BIC runs its own call, most with two to four cut-offs per year (commonly spring and autumn). There is almost always an open ESA BIC call somewhere in Europe.

procedure_steps.detail: Choose the ESA BIC in the country/region where you will be based
Check that your product has a genuine space link (space technology used on Earth, or a downstream service using satellite data/navigation/communications)
Submit the BIC application form and business plan by the local cut-off
Technical and business review, then jury interview
Incubation agreement and start of the two-year programme

documents_required.doc: Business plan
Description of the space technology link
Financial projections
Company registration or intent to incorporate
documents_required.note: Some BICs accept pre-incorporation teams

eligibility.other_note: Entrepreneurs developing applications that use space-based systems, use space technologies in a non-space domain, or innovative products/services for the space sector; apply to an individual ESA BIC before its cut-off date (a company can be registered at contract signing).

programmes.source_snippet: Up to two years of business incubation at an ESA BIC of your choice. EUR 50k equity free funding for product and IP development.

programmes.name_en: ESA Business Incubation Centre network
programmes.funder: European Space Agency (ESA) with national and regional co-funders
programmes.amount_note: EUR 50,000 equity-free funding for product and IP development, plus up to two years of incubation, technical support from ESA experts, business coaching, legal and IPR advice and fundraising support.
programmes.deadline_note: Each ESA BIC runs its own call cycle with published cut-off dates, typically two to four per year. 36 centres across 23 European countries with over 100 locations; more than 2,000 startups supported.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact the local ESA BIC to discuss whether the business idea fits
Submit the completed application documents before the announced local deadline
Applications are reviewed by a Tender Opening Board
Shortlisted applicants present to a Tender Evaluation Board
On approval, register a company before signing the incubation contract

documents_required.doc: Business plan
Technical description of the space link
Financial plan
Founder CVs

eligibility.other_note: Business must either use space-based systems (satellite navigation, Earth observation, satellite communication), use space technologies in a non-space domain, or develop innovative products and services for the space sector. Company must be registered in the host country before contract signature; companies must normally be younger than five years.

programmes.source_snippet: Up to two years of business incubation at an ESA BIC of your choice. EUR 50k equity free funding for product and IP development.

programmes.name_en: ESA Space Solutions Kick-start Activity
programmes.funder: European Space Agency (ESA Space Solutions / Business Applications)
programmes.amount_note: Kick-starts (six-month feasibility studies) are funded at 75%, ESA up to EUR 75,000 per contract, maximum total activity cost EUR 100,000.
programmes.deadline_note: Open call, apply any time; proposals evaluated in batches. 2026 batch deadlines: 27 Feb, 27 Mar, 29 May, 28 Aug, 30 Oct 2026 (13:00 CET).

eligibility.other_note: Applicant must be registered in an ESA Member State that subscribes to the Business Applications programme, and the national delegation must endorse the activity.

programmes.source_snippet: Kick-start activities will be funded at 75%, with ESA providing up to EUR 75,000 per contract. The maximum total cost of a Kick-start activity is EUR 100,000.

programmes.name_en: ESA Space Solutions Demonstration Projects
programmes.funder: European Space Agency, Directorate of Commercialisation, Industry and Procurement
programmes.amount_note: Open Call for Proof-of-concept Studies (activity cost up to EUR 600,000) and Pilot Projects (case-by-case). ESA co-funding: baseline up to 75% (PoC) / 50% (pilots); micro, small and medium businesses up to 80%, depending on national delegation authorisation.
programmes.deadline_note: Always-open invitation to apply; no fixed deadline.

eligibility.other_note: Registered in a participating ESA Member State with national delegation authorisation. Requires committed pilot users and a credible route to commercial operation.

programmes.source_snippet: This is an Open Call for Proposals, meaning that it is an always open invitation for businesses to apply for a funding activity relating to a space-enabled application or service for any industry, market or topic.

programmes.name_en: ESA InCubed (Investing in Industrial Innovation, Earth observation)
programmes.funder: European Space Agency Phi-lab / Earth Observation Programmes
programmes.amount_note: Co-funds the development of commercial Earth observation products and services. ESA typically covers up to 50-80% of project cost depending on the company's size and the maturity of the product, with the applicant funding the rest. Project sizes are negotiated case by case and have ranged widely.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuously open: InCubed accepts ideas at any time through its online idea submission, followed by a structured proposal phase.

eligibility.other_note: Company registered in an ESA Member State participating in the InCubed programme. Requires a commercial Earth observation product with a clear business case and co-investment.

Apply for financing directly to that bank, guarantee body or fund
The intermediary applies the InvestEU-backed terms (reduced collateral, longer tenor or lower rate) as part of its normal credit process

eligibility.other_note: SME or small mid-cap established in an EU Member State. Final eligibility and pricing are set by the intermediary.

programmes.funder: Eureka Network / European Partnership on Innovative SMEs, co-funded by Horizon Europe and by national funding bodies
programmes.amount_note: There is no single Eurostars grant amount. Funding is decentralised: participants receive money 'directly from National Funding Bodies', and each national agency sets its own 'funding rate per type of company' and eligible costs. Applicants must check their National Funding Body's rules. Projects must run 36 months or less.
programmes.deadline_note: Two cut-offs per year, typically March and September. Call 11 (deadline 10 September 2026) has closed. Eurostars Call 12 is open, deadline 4 March 2027, per eurekanetwork.org.

procedure_steps.detail: Build a consortium led by an innovative SME from a Eurostars country, with at least two independent entities from at least two Eurostars countries (one must be an EU or Horizon Europe Associated Country).
Contact your National Funding Body to understand national funding rates, eligible costs and any national procedures before submitting.
Submit the joint project application online by the cut-off date; central Eureka evaluation is followed by national funding decisions.

documents_required.doc: Joint project application (consortium project description, workplan, budget)
National forms required by each participant's National Funding Body
documents_required.note: Varies by country

documents_required.doc: SME self-declaration
documents_required.note: SME status per Recommendation 2003/361/EC

Because money comes from national budgets, individual national awards may be granted under GBER or under de minimis - check the national body.

programmes.source_snippet: The project consortium must be led by an innovative SME from a Eurostars country. ... The budget of the SMEs from the Eurostars countries (excluding any subcontracting) is 50% or more of the total project cost.

programmes.name_en: InvestEU Programme
programmes.funder: European Commission with the European Investment Bank (EIB) Group and other implementing partners
programmes.amount_note: InvestEU is not a grant programme. It provides 'an EU budget guarantee of €26.2 billion' intended to mobilise at least EUR 372 billion in additional investment over 2021-27. Companies never receive money directly from InvestEU: 'The InvestEU Fund is implemented through financial partners that will invest in projects.' Ticket sizes and terms are set by each intermediary bank, fund or guarantee scheme.
programmes.deadline_note: No EU-level deadline. Access is continuous through intermediaries; each intermediary has its own process and timing.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify an InvestEU implementing partner or financial intermediary operating in your country (EIB Group, national promotional bank, VC fund or commercial lender with an InvestEU guarantee).
Apply directly to that intermediary under its own credit or investment process; the InvestEU guarantee sits behind the product and is usually invisible to the borrower.

documents_required.doc: Whatever the financial intermediary requires (business plan, financial statements, security)
documents_required.note: Set by the intermediary, not by the Commission

Important for aggregators: InvestEU is debt/equity/guarantee, not a grant, and there is no direct application to the Commission. Where an InvestEU-backed product is delivered by a national intermediary on below-market terms, the aid element may be granted to the SME under de minimis or GBER at national level - ask the intermediary for the de minimis certificate.

programmes.source_snippet: The InvestEU Programme supports sustainable investment, innovation and job creation in Europe. ... The InvestEU Fund is implemented through financial partners that will invest in projects.
